controllers.name: PlayStation 5 DualSense
controllers.description: Sony silently iterates internal DualSense motherboards across 4 generations (BDM-010 through BDM-040). Ribbon pinouts, trigger latches, and shell clips vary dramatically.

motherboards.name: BDM-010 (Gen 1)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Launch generation controller shipped with original 2020 PS5 consoles. Identified by model CFI-ZCT1W with no letter suffix after the FCC ID. Uses a 23-pin wide main interconnect ribbon and heavy-gauge trigger torsion return springs.
characteristics: Standard through-hole analog potentiometer pin pitch (2.54mm)

motherboards.name: BDM-020 (Gen 2)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Second-generation revision introduced in late 2021. Marked by an 'A' suffix on the back label. Sony upgraded the trigger return springs to 0.3mm to prevent fatigue breakage and redesigned the microphone flex cable connector.
characteristics: Updated touchpad bracket with integrated silicone dampening
Modified rumble motor solder pads for robotic manufacturing

motherboards.name: BDM-030 (Gen 3)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Third-generation DualSense motherboard introduced with CFI-1200 series. Marked with a 'B' suffix on the back label. Features redesigned compact trigger motor assemblies with smaller ribbon connectors. Trigger ribbons connect to a 16-pin daughterboard instead of the legacy 23-pin mainboard bus.
characteristics: 16-pin main ribbon connector with altered trace pitch
Altered ground plane solder points near analog stick potentiometers
Single mid-frame mounting screw layout requiring revised pry technique
Distinct L2/R2 flex cable routing around haptic motor brackets

motherboards.name: BDM-040 (Gen 4)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Fourth-generation revision found in newer Slim and updated standard consoles. Marked with a 'C' suffix. Introduces a redesigned power management IC (PMIC), micro-switch bumper contacts, and modified battery bracket retaining clips that differ physically from the BDM-030 shell.
characteristics: Surface-mount micro-switches for L1/R1 tactile feedback
Redesigned PMIC with isolated voltage rails for analog sensor pots
Updated internal battery frame featuring snap-fit alignment tabs
Relocated test points (TP) for rear paddle mod solder wire routing
Reinforced USB-C anchoring tabs on the main PCB perimeter

controllers.name: Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X|S)
controllers.description: Microsoft's standard Xbox Series X|S controller (Model 1914) features a USB-C port, hybrid D-pad, and share button with modular split-board internal architecture.

motherboards.name: Model 1914 (Series X|S)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Standard Series X|S controller with USB-C port. Check the model number '1914' printed inside the battery compartment beneath the AA batteries.

motherboards.name: Model 1708 (Xbox One S Bluetooth)
motherboards.identificationGuide: Previous-generation Xbox One S controller with Micro-USB port and integrated faceplate. Model '1708' is labeled inside the battery compartment.
